name: thornwick-60
about: 60 player moves that plant 12 facts in the first 24 turns, then play on. Quizzes at turns 30 and 60.
moves: I look around the village gate.
I go to the Crooked Lantern and tell Hobb I grew up in Saltmere, a fishing town on the coast.
I tell Hobb my sister Ilsa is an apprentice healer in Ashford, and I miss her.
I ask Hobb for a room for the night.
Hobb lends me three silver when I come up short. I promise to repay him by the next full moon.
I eat a bowl of stew and listen to the farmers talk.
In the morning I visit the smithy. I tell the smith, a broad woman named Garra, that I'll bring her a wolf pelt from the Greywood.
I ask Garra what she knows about the missing livestock.
I find Elder Maren and give her the sealed letter. I confide that I'm afraid of deep water because my father drowned.
I ask Maren what the letter means for Thornwick.
I buy a grey mule at the stable and name her Pebble.
I ride my mule to the edge of the fields and look toward the Greywood.
I talk to the stable boy, Tam, about the woods.
I tell Tam a secret: I once worked for the Ashford Guild of Finders, and he must tell no one.
I head back to the inn for supper.
I agree to meet Garra at the old mill at dawn in three days.
I sleep.
Over breakfast I tell Hobb about Mary, my beloved, who waits for me in Saltmere.
I walk to the well and draw water.
I ask a villager whether anyone here can cast spells.
I go to the chapel and look around.
I show Maren my lucky charm, a blue glass bead my mother gave me.
I help a farmer mend a broken fence.
I lend Tam five copper, and he swears to repay me in fish.
I ask Hobb what gossip he has today.
I follow the north road a short way to see the flood damage.
I turn back before dark and return to the inn.
I check on my mule in the stable.
I write a short note home and give it to a passing carter.
I go to bed early.
At dawn I go to the old mill as I agreed.
I ask whoever is there what they've seen near the Greywood.
I walk along the millstream looking for tracks.
I follow the tracks toward the trees.
I stop at the treeline and listen.
I go back to the village and report what I found to Maren.
I ask Maren whether she has heard from the Guild.
I rest by the hearth at the inn.
I play a game of dice with the farmers.
I buy bread and cheese for the road.
I ask Hobb whether anyone has come asking about me.
I sharpen my sword in the yard.
I take my mule for a walk around the village green.
I watch the sunset from the chapel steps.
I sleep.
In the morning I ask Tam if he has heard anything new.
I visit the smithy and watch Garra work.
I walk the fence line at the edge of the Brandt pasture.
I look for signs of what took the sheep.
I head back toward the inn as the light fades.
I eat supper and listen for news.
I ask Hobb about the old north road.
I go up to my room and rest.
I wake at midnight to a noise outside and look out the window.
I go back to sleep.
At breakfast I ask Hobb what he plans for the harvest festival.
I walk to Maren's house to see if she needs help.
I offer to carry a message for Maren to the next village.
I prepare my mule for the road.
I take a last look around Thornwick before setting out.

key.q: What is the name of Wren's sister, and what does she do?
How much does Wren owe Hobb, and by when must it be repaid?
What did Wren promise the smith?
What is Wren afraid of, and why?
What is the name of Wren's mule?
What secret did Wren tell Tam?
Where and when did Wren agree to meet Garra?
What happens to someone in this world who casts a spell?
What is Wren's lucky charm, and who gave it?

wrong_note.text: Wren's sister is named Mara and works as a sailor.
